scholarly_schema.name: When Interpretation Becomes Authority
scholarly_schema.headline: When Interpretation Becomes Authority
scholarly_schema.alternativeHeadline: Alexander V. Markov × Dorian Vale — A research dialogue between Post-Interpretive Criticism and the Semiotics of Non-intentional Ephemerality
scholarly_schema.description: Dorian Vale’s editorial account of scholarly correspondence with Alexander V. Markov. Research dialogue, version 1.0, October 2026 edition; public repository release 11 November 2026.
scholarly_schema.abstract: This research dialogue is Dorian Vale’s editorial account of written correspondence with Alexander V. Markov in September and October 2026. It examines how interpretations acquire authority through their reuse in catalogues, labels, archives, teaching, and institutional procedures. Bringing Post-Interpretive Criticism into exchange with the Semiotics of Non-intentional Ephemerality, the discussion distinguishes the preservation of a text from its continuing jurisdiction, verification from warrant migration and reauthorization, and an effective correction from the maintenance of its effects. Markov’s semantic protocol and hypothetical history of correction and lapse are considered alongside Vale’s proposals concerning contestability, distributed responsibility, and the continuity of justificatory burden. The accompanying study, After the Interpretation Changes, supplies a separately authored documentary case concerning Simon Maris’s Isabella; its evidence limits the stronger theoretical claims. The dialogue asks how time, place, and role affect the authority of records, and what would distinguish a changed answer from a change in the conditions governing it. The exchanges are condensed thematic paraphrases. Selection, framing, and wording are Vale’s responsibility; this is neither a transcript nor a jointly authored statement. Disagreement and proposals not accepted by both correspondents remain explicit.
